title: Embed/rerank outage retrospective: KV cache hotspot after model-variant rollout
creator: Aisha Ng
summary: On 2026-03-10 we observed a sustained throughput and latency degradation for the embeddings + rerank endpoints after a staged rollout of a new quantized model variant and an accompanying kernel selector change. The outage affected ~22% of requests globally; key customer-facing services experienced tail-latency regressions and partial request drops. This ticket documents timeline, root causes, mitigations, and follow-up actions.
incident_timeline: 2026-03-10 02:50 UTC - Canary rollout of model v2-quant initiated in region us-west-2 with kernel-selector v5 enabled.
2026-03-10 03:12 UTC - Grafana alert: embeddings.rerank.avg_latency_99 > 1200ms for 3m. Pager triggered (oncall SRE team).
2026-03-10 03:15 UTC - Error budget notifications; observed 40% drop in processed queries on affected pools and error rate increase to 2.8% (baseline 0.1%).
2026-03-10 03:25 UTC - Incident commander (Aisha) assembled SRE + runtime + model-ops + infra. Initial hypothesis: autoscaler flapping during rollout.
2026-03-10 03:40 UTC - Production tracing showed increased KV cache eviction rates correlated with high CPU sys time on runtime workers serving quantized shards.
2026-03-10 04:05 UTC - Emergency mitigation: rollback kernel-selector v5 to v4 on canaries and pin model to v1-stable for remaining nodes in us-west-2. Began gradual scale-up of dedicated pools.
2026-03-10 05:10 UTC - Latency returned to baseline for most traffic; error rate fell to 0.12%.
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC - Full rollback confirmed across regions; incident declared mitigated. Post-incident follow-up meeting scheduled.
2026-03-11 11:00 UTC - Post-incident retrospective held; action items assigned.
detection: Automated latency SLO alerts (99th percentile) fired in Grafana with a correlated rise in KV cache eviction metrics and CPU utilization on runtime processes. Customers reported increased request timeouts via support channels.
impact: Approximately 22% of rerank/embedding requests routed to canary pools experienced elevated latency (p99 up to 1.8s) and a small fraction (0.5% absolute) observed 5xx responses due to internal throttling. Several enterprise customers using synchronous rerank flows reported degraded UX during the window.
metrics: Throughput on affected pools: 40% reduction in qps for 35 minutes
KV cache eviction rate: +320% vs baseline
CPU sys time on runtime worker: +60%
root_cause: A combination of (1) a new quantized model variant (v2-quant) that changed attention/key/value memory access patterns, (2) kernel-selector v5 enabling a different batching/kernel path that increased per-process memory pressure, and (3) autoscaler health checks that considered transient queue depth as signal to drain and scale down nodes. Together these produced frequent KV cache evictions and CPU contention on a subset of shards, which reduced effective capacity and increased tail latency.
contributing_factors: Model-ops rollout did not include a stress test for KV cache churn under realistic sequence length mix.
Kernel-selector change lacked a preflight canary that measured KV cache eviction metrics specifically.
Autoscaler health heuristic uses queue depth thresholds that were sensitive to temporary latency spikes caused by cache pressure; this triggered unnecessary drains.
Lack of a configured fallback to a compatible non-quantized model for rerank endpoints in the rollout pipeline.
immediate_mitigations: Reverted kernel-selector v5 to v4 on canary and then all affected pools (runtime PR #4271).
Pinned serving config to v1-stable model for production pools while investigation proceeded.
Manually increased shard capacity by adding 2 nodes to affected dedicated pools to reduce eviction frequency.
Enabled temporary rate-limiting on lower-priority batched rerank requests to protect synchronous customer traffic.
long_term_mitigations: Add KV cache churn and eviction rate to preflight canary dashboards and gate kernel-selector/model rollouts on these metrics (action: create canary metric set).
Introduce a model-compatibility test in the onboard pipeline that runs a small workload with representative sequence lengths and measures cache pressure and kernel CPU characteristics.
Harden autoscaler health checks to ignore short-lived queue depth spikes and instead use aggregated latency + CPU metrics before node drain decisions.
Implement automatic model fallback policy: if cache-eviction > X% or p99 latency > Y for 5m, route to last-known-compatible model variant.
Improve runtime telemetry: expose per-shard KV cache hits/evicts and per-kernel CPU breakdown to Grafana.
validation_and_postdeploy: Created a synthetic workload harness that emulates high-token, mixed-sequence rerank traffic; validated that kernel-selector v5 with model v2-quant still causes higher eviction — blocked in CI until mitigations added (CI job: embed-rerank-canary).
Added canary job to deploy candidate runtime changes to a single non-customer-facing pool with kv-eviction monitoring enabled.
Rollout playbook updated to include KV eviction threshold checks and mandatory 30m observation period before cross-region rollout.

notes: Blameless postmortem — root cause analysis focuses on process and instrumentation gaps.
We observed that quantized models change memory access patterns in ways that are not caught by token-only performance tests; integrate memory/caching measurements into model evaluation.
Customer communication: PMs to coordinate targeted emails to top 10 affected customers; generic status update posted to status.redwood.ai.
